subQuests.subQuestName: Have a conversation on the train

771600301.text: It's so cold out there... The train's definitely much cozier...

771600302.text: That is precisely why the trains exist. Trekking long distances through such bitter cold would hardly be good for anyone's health.

771600303.text: Perhaps that, too, was my creator's original purpose in establishing it... After all, this land of ice and snow is hardly a place fit for humans to survive.

771600304.text: Your creator...? Ah, could that be the strange woman we ran into earlier?

771600305.text: How rude! What do you mean, "strange woman"!?

771600306.text: Paimon definitely doesn't mean the strange woman you're talking about right now!

771600307.text: ...You know, the one who appeared in that mumbly-jumbly town with the firebird, and in that castle full of Snegovik. Paimon remembers her name was Ak...

771600308.text: Miss Aksinya, yes. Judging from the memories I have recovered so far, she was once a member of the Belyi Tsar's research organization, the Aly{RUBY#[S]Hvergelmir}pium...

771600309.text: She created me so that I might... guide a certain mighty power, and create a "Tomorrow" — a world where no one would ever suffer again...

771600310.text: A land that has cast aside envy, hatred, and selfish desire. A "Courtyard of Carefree Light" held aloft by the hands of all living beings. Thus...

771600311.text: "Thus shall a radiant world descend, where there will be no distinction between human and human, nor between human and god."

771600312.text: A world where there's no distinction between humans and gods? Hmm... Paimon can't even imagine how you'd make that happen...

771600313.text: "A pure world of mankind, where gods need not wield divine power, and humans need not rely on gods."

771600314.text: ...That is the outcome of the plan, as I remember it.

771600315.text: But as for how it was to be accomplished... I'm sorry, but I do not know the full scope of the final plan. To the plan as a whole, I was nothing more than a "tool" within it.

771600316.text: Oh, Paimon gets it! Goggles is like a crafting bench. It can craft all kinds of amazing things, but a crafting bench doesn't run around eating up its own materials.

771600317.text: That is a very apt analogy. However, if I may, Miss Paimon, in present-day Snezhnaya, alchemy is not an officially supported field of study...

771600318.text: R-Right... But, well, we're on our own train, so...

771600319.text: ...But should I reclaim my body? Once I do, that means I must complete my mission... "The Courtyard of Carefree Light"...

771600320.text: What if, after my memories are restored, I find that these are not the ones I wished to recover? What should I do then?

771600321.text: What if... What if that's the only reason I was created, the purpose I was destined for...?

771600323.text: Yeah! It's definitely not good to decide when you don't know anything yet. No matter what, you've gotta remember everything first!

771600327.text: Anyway... Goggles has helped us out a lot! Even if that wasn't what Goggles was originally created for, Goggles has still been really useful to us!

771600328.text: When that time comes, just come back to us.

771600330.text: Besides, we already talked about all the things we're going to do together when you get your body back! Warming up by the fire, having snowball fights, running around on the ice fields... We promised!

771600331.text: Yes. I look forward to... adventuring together with you both after I recover my body.

771600332.text: Though I have thought this countless times throughout our journey... I am truly glad that you were the one to bring me out of that place, and that I was able to meet you both.

771600333.text: Let's go. It is time to go to the "Courtyard of Carefree Light," to the door that waits to be opened.

771600325.text: Exactly! And if anyone's to blame, it's whoever misused the crafting bench!

771600326.text: Wah, this is all your fault... Now Paimon can't stop imagining a crafting bench going "huff, huff" like some kind of dog!

subQuests.subQuestName: Open the door leading to the Courtyard of Carefree Light

771600101.text: This is where the entrance to the Courtyard of Carefree Light is. Should I try to return my powers to this place and open the gate...?

771600103.text: Let's perform the return ceremony then, and open the gate to the courtyard...

771600105.text: Yes. It may be better to come back to this when you're more prepared.

771600201.text: We're finally in. That felt really cold just now.

771600202.text: We should be able to reconstruct Goggles' body, now right? ...Hold on, where's Goggles?

771600205.text: What's going on!? Even those blue lenses have disappeared...

771600206.text: There is no cause for concern... The once-fragmented body, along with the consciousness bound to inanimate matter, have all returned to where they rightfully belong.

771600207.text: You may leave the Eye of Graeae in my keeping for a time. In my estimation, it is a form of homecoming for it anyhow.

771600209.text: Yes. I'm glad to see that you remember my name, Paimon.

771600211.text: Don't worry, he will come to. Just maybe not so soon, that's all.

771600212.text: Oh, so he's getting his body back, right? Good as new? He'll be back to his original human form?

771600213.text: No, he will not. He will inhabit "another's form" and metamorphose into the true "Proto-Man." I suppose this might be slightly different from what you imagined.

771600214.text: Hold on... This is all a little confusing. Didn't he want his old body back?

771600216.text: He knows nothing because he has completely forgotten the past. To think that "reclaiming his old body" is the only thought driving him... Perhaps that in itself is a cruelty.

771600217.text: But reclaiming his old body was never his true purpose from the beginning. That was all merely preparation for assimilating into, and reforging, a form of an even higher order.

771600218.text: This is something he should come to comprehend once his memory is made whole.

771600219.text: "Assimilating and being changed into a form of an even higher order..." Eh, are you saying that his body and powers will all go into someone else's body?

771600221.text: But how is that gonna happen when his body's already gone...?

771600601.text: It's done. Now, all we have to do is... wait a little while longer...

771600602.text: Wha... What is that? It's huge, and kinda weird, too...

771600603.text: Wait, no, that's not the point!

771600604.text: You're being so horrible, Aksinya! Just give us back Goggles!

771600605.text: Looks like the two of you are really fond of the Eye of Graeae... If only my former colleague was able to see the value of this creation as well.

771600606.text: ...Although the physical body has begun to transform, the consciousness has yet to take root... His Majesty...

771600608.text: This was the original body of the Tsar. But it would change into the form of a fae whenever speaking with us or traveling alongside other fae.

771600609.text: Unable to maintain his avatar after death, he reverted to his original state, a magnificent, almost transcendental form.

771600610.text: Have I ever told you this before? That the faces of the Proto-Man were actually modeled after the visage of His Majesty the Belyi Tsar's human manifestation?

771600612.text: Mmhmm! Paimon has zero interest in whatever you were babbling on about just now...

771600614.text: The Eye of Graeae was always built to host the Proto-Man's consciousness... Such that he would not disappear after offering his flesh and blood to His Majesty...

771600615.text: It was originally meant to preserve "him."

771600616.text: Now, since it is no longer useful to me, I shall therefore make a gift of it to you. I trust that you will find a good use for it.

771600619.text: Restored to original state. The {RUBY#[D]Eye of Graeae} is now at your service...

771600621.text: This isn't Goggles at all! This is just... a tool. It's nothing more than an empty shell!

771600622.text: I'm sorry. Its consciousness should already be part of the Primordial Human by now, to serve as the core of the Velikan {RUBY#[S]Svarod}of Light.

771600623.text: This is something I am unable to return to you. But don't worry, you will no longer grieve this soon, since...

771600625.text: Because the Primordial Human has awoken.

771600628.text: Yes, it is I... I now remember everything. Much time has passed... both for you, Aksinya, and for me.

771600629.text: Fate truly is absurd. This is exactly the scenario that I strove to avoid when I was still in my prototypical form.

771600630.text: That's just how fate is. It pushes you to the cliff's edge, like the worst of nemeses.

771600631.text: A situation you had to avoid...?

771600632.text: Yes, and that is why I tried to persuade Koshchei, Pavlina, and Alvis to stop her before she decided to begin the final experiment.

771600633.text: After all, the authority that the Primordial Human wields may as well be a deadly{RUBY#[D]Ether} venom to humans and fae, who carry mixed desires within them...

771600634.text: Wait... So that blue algae thing, that Snegurochka, and the Domovoy Grand Duke from Novokitezhgrad... They betrayed Aksinya because of you?

771600636.text: I promised them they could both stop Aksinya in and gain what they wanted in this way.

771600637.text: Each of them was driven in their own way by ideals, or perhaps ambitions, that would see them transcend all life. This proved simple to use.

771600638.text: By contrast, our dear Aksinya, our lovely Aksinya... The resolve she possessed seemed all the more unusual, did it not?

771600639.text: And so, I incited them to divide me up, to split me into pieces, and to betray Aksinya...

771600640.text: For if I were to become the Primordial Human, become a transcendent one... Just as I am now... That would mean that the world was about to undergo an inexorable revolution.

771600641.text: The "beast" mocked me, for it believed its mission fulfilled. And I, despite fleeing my duties with all my mind, wound up here all the same.

771600645.text: You left no place for yourself in the world that would be born from these fresh schematics, did you?

771600647.text: ...Yes. I am willing to believe in a nation of love everlasting. I believed in His Majesty the Tsar, and in his wish.

771600648.text: But those who have lost faith in love must be banished from the new world, the realm of eternal love. I do not have the right to enter that world.

771600649.text: Banishment? It is more akin to being slain, I rate. Eternal love, eternal overflow, eternal joy... Those who trust not to love and joy cannot enter this realm.

771600650.text: But it is precisely one who does not trust either who could fashion such a cruel plan. This, the "loving" Belyi Tsar had long realized.

771600651.text: And that is why he is great. He chose me. This is my duty, my sole purpose for living. Even if I cannot step into the new world...

771600652.text: I wish to see its descent with my own eyes, to see it rise from a cornerstone forged from my corpse.

771600653.text: ...And as for you? Do you still believe that an eternity of love can be attained without His Majesty's plan?

771600654.text: Alvis, Koshschei, and Pavlina... Their pursuits have melted away like snow... None can resist the erosion of time, the withering of the spirit, the shriveling of dreams.

771600655.text: So many have given up so much in the fight to keep a joyous spirit... But none have succeeded.

771600656.text: What choice can you make at this point?

771600657.text: None. You know this as well, Aksinya, that I could not refuse you once I had recalled all, what more, now that I have become the Primordial Human.

771600658.text: Wait, Goggles... Are you really gonna open the gate to the Courtyard of Carefree Light?

771600660.text: You have my utmost thanks, you two, for giving me the chance to give up even at this stage.

771600661.text: But... Alas, I cannot let her plans come to naught. So, if you wish not to see this come to pass... Please, stop both of us.

771600662.text: #But before that, {NICKNAME}, I would like to show Aksinya something... I'd like you to answer a question of mine.

771600663.text: #You seek your sibling, and you have traveled the world to understand {M#her}{F#him}, to seek the things that you missed out experiencing alongside {M#her}{F#him}, to stand before {M#her}{F#him}.

771600664.text: #But if the gap between you is too great, and you, in the end, find that {M#she}{F#he} is not what you imagined, that your once-beloved kin is kin no longer...

771600665.text: #That {M#she}{F#he} has changed and become another person, someone you never imagined {M#she}{F#he} might...

771600666.text: #What!? Why would that ever happen? {NICKNAME}'s {M#sister}{F#brother} wouldn't change!

771600667.text: This is but a hypothetical scenario. Do not be alarmed, Paimon.

771600668.text: #What would you do, {NICKNAME}? I'd... like to know your answer.

771600670.text: #Then I will learn to love {M#her}{F#him} once again...

771600671.text: No matter how many times I have to do it.

771600673.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}. That was wonderful. Better by far than any answer I imagined I would get.

771600674.text: The time has come, and the Courtyard shall soon activate. It is a shame...

771600675.text: "But what's to be done? Whomsoever loves should share the burden of destiny with the ones he loves."

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way out of the situation
Find a way out of the situation
Follow the path to get behind the Primordial Human
Remove the nerves from the train

771601501.text: ...At the end of the day, I haven't been able to do anything in time...

771601502.text: Ah, what a shame... This was the sole great endeavor I was meant to undertake...

771601503.text: As I see it, you have done enough... You endured the passage of time for so long, even in such a place.

771601504.text: Your ambition burned so strongly that even the branches of fate had to bend low for you... To the point where you could escape from this place.

771601505.text: In truth, my escape from the Shadow Realm was largely thanks to Izmaylov's aid. He said it was the last thing he could do for me.

771601506.text: And yet, I still failed... and lost everything... and where are we falling to now?

771601507.text: Perhaps we shall fall into the endless depths of the Shadow Realm, tumbling for five hundred years, and another five thereafter.

771601508.text: But this is already the best possible ending I could face.

771601510.text: Yes, Aksinya. Here, there is no "His Majesty, the Belyi Tsar." No "Primordial Human." Here, there is no court jester of Snezhnaya, no Snegurochka, no other fae.

771601511.text: Here, there is only you and me. Here... we do not even need names.

771601513.text: ...Yes, it is indeed. This is good — to be within this shadowy realm, a world as small as a walnut shell. Just the two of us, at the very end.

771601514.text: ...I once thought that I could never be worthy of setting foot in a world like this...

771601515.text: #...You know, {NICKNAME} is right. Why should we fear love's fading, that we should insist that it stand eternally?

771601516.text: One who dares to believe in love will not be obsessed with its disappearance... and if I believe in it, so what if I should lose it?

771601517.text: I'd climb back up, shake the dust and dirt free, head off in pursuit once more, to take hold, to go forth, to love again!

771601518.text: Why did I... Why did I want to...

771601520.text: *sigh* ...I once hated this world, imprisoned as it was within an eggshell. Yet in the end, all I did was build another shell.

771601521.text: Perhaps that is just how fate has been from the start, pushing you to the cliff's edge, like the worst of nemeses.

771601522.text: Heh. Never thought you'd be the one to say that to me.

771601523.text: ...I was once driven to such fury when I learned the truth of the world, and bearing that indignation, I asked the Tsar:

771601524.text: "What is the point of an egg that does not allow the life within it to emerge from the shell? Why does it exist in this universe at all?"

771601525.text: But I never received the answer I wished to have from him.

771601526.text: So that was a thought you once had. I see.

771601527.text: What about now, Aksinya? Do you still think this way? You've done so much... Did you ever find an answer to that question?

771601528.text: More or less, I suppose. The answer is... *sigh* Y—You already know the answer, don't you?

771601529.text: ...You once considered me far too selfish.

771601530.text: But no matter what form love takes, whether it gives or takes possession, outward expressions of love always reflect what lies within in some way.

771601531.text: To love the world is to love yourself...

771601532.text: But this is also a great thing, because this is how the world is, and one's desire to be saved must be strong enough to save the world entire.

771601533.text: I'd always believed that I should love myself first, and then the world, or I would fall into error, just as I have today.

771601534.text: But you... you are truly magnificent, Aksinya.

771601536.text: Ah, I am hurt. That came from the bottom of my heart.

771601538.text: Yes. Everything... Pavlina, Koshchei, Alvis, you... and... and His Majesty the Tsar... all the things you wanted...

771601539.text: Why am I only now realizing that I, too... once longed for those things...

771601601.text: Oof, finally! We've finally made it out of that Shadow Realm!

771601602.text: Hang on, Paimon doesn't see Goggles or Aksinya... and the Belyi Tsar's body is missing, too. Where have they gone to?

771601603.text: I don't think we'll ever see them again...

771601604.text: Huh. Do you think it's possible that Goggles might actually be hiding inside that mechanism Aksinya gave you?

771601605.text: You know how it's like in those shows? They make you think that someone's vanished forever, and then, POOF! They pop up right in front of you again.

771601606.text: How about you let Paimon take a look?

771601607.text: And so, Paimon makes several attempts at "cracking" the mechanism.\nBut the only voice that answers is a cold, lifeless one.\nThis is how the two of you learn that while "Goggles" has retained some of its abilities, it really is nothing more than, well, a pair of goggles at this point.

771601608.text: He's... really fallen into that deep, deep hole...

771601609.text: But that's his own fault for choosing to open the door to that Courtyard of Carefree Light or whatever... But... Paimon thinks he was pretty cool when he chose to help Aksinya.

771601610.text: Heh, even if one day the whole world were to turn against you, Paimon would stand by you no matter what!

771601611.text: And I'll do the same for you, Paimon.

771601613.text: Hmm.. You know, now that the Belyi Tsar's body has gone missing... We're gonna be in big trouble if someone sees us now!

771601614.text: We've got to get out of here, fast!
